chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: The Tennessee 10 and a fired job in Atlantic City
summary: As a student he went to Atlantic City, formed a band that starved, and was fired at Charlie Johnson's Paradise when he could not read the show.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I worked in Atlantic City, during the -- when I was in school. There was a fellow in Mahari there -- did a lot of work in trombone player by the name of (inaudible) Atlantic City, so he took me to Atlantic City around '25.

And he said, we'll get a band out there, so we organized a little band in Atlantic City called the Tennessee 10. And we didn't get any work. We starved to death. So I -- someone took me over to the Paradise where Charlie Johnson had his band and I went there on tenor saxophone and I played everything -- was lovely until the show, and when the show came on, I naturally couldn't read so they fired me right away. And then I went -- I was pushing chairs on the Boardwalk, hopping bells at night.
Yes. And I stayed there till I went back to school. That was just one of the crazy things that happened.
